correctness.rationale: The proof computes all spectral subspaces and their dimensions from the graph matrix, uses exact zero-mode comparison and the nonzero supports of pair vertices; it treats the m=2 last-cell pair separately, whose transverse projection vanishes but whose second-plane negative eigenvalue coincides with the transverse eigenvalue to show pair-only transfer, and solves all required eigenphases via odd-integer divisibility. The equality d=m+2r-2 yields iff r odd and m=2 mod 4; U=I-2P_zero gives the complete cell-block unitary. The finite exact rational checker confirms 84 graph matrices, kernel projectors and phase solvability. No infinite statement is inferred from those tests.

originality.rationale: The motivating normalized-Laplacian phase criterion, existing strong-cospectral twin theorem, and general multipartite spectrum were inspected and credited. The assessed novel content is the exact joint arithmetic iff, complete transfer time set and global simultaneous-swap-plus-reflection propagator for the full including irregular family; regular m=2 boundary is already substantially covered by other work. Statement implication comparisons and exact searches found no known dominating transfer classification, though equivalent weakly indexed work remains a risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent result may exist under quotient-graph, Grover-reflection, or twin-class terminology and evade indexing.

The directly linked publisher version of the 2020 complete-multipartite spectral paper was not accessible as an unbroken full document; relevant indexed full-text theorem and sections were read, and there is no positive evidence of a PST claim there.

General known spectral and phase theorems make the result derivable in principle; novelty concerns the motivated explicit all-parameter classification and whole-network unitary, not those building blocks.

value.rationale: Complete natural two-parameter classification for an exact normalized-Laplacian quantum routing architecture; determines all success/failure cases, pair locations, earliest/all exact times, and a simultaneous multimode swap with a reflection. The 12-vertex irregular witness K_{2,2,2,6} proves that the classification yields behavior outside regular-base double-cone examples. There is genuine normalized-degree dependence and an eigenmode boundary at r=1; the result is neither an arbitrary finite slice nor a routine numerical recomputation.
